primary_sources.supports: DataRow/command completion and transaction success are distinct protocol events; unexpected connection termination rolls back an open transaction, with caveat about already-processing work. Native fault stops before COMMIT or withholds a real successful reply.
Read Committed own writes visible before commit; concurrent updater waits and sees whether earlier update committed or rolled back. A current row cannot identify a discarded application attempt.
FOR UPDATE waits then locks/returns current updated row; locks end with transaction. Locking reveals state, rather than recovering an independently identified claim.

design_inference: Abandoning an uncertain claim is the chosen application contract. It follows from never authorising work with a provisional token, not from a PostgreSQL ownership-recovery feature. Native verifier records its actual effects and counterexample.
